headline: The shop is real. The map is arguing with itself.
summary: Stacey is easy to like in person. Online, a neighbor has to guess which address is yours, which hours are true, and whether the website even belongs to the shop. That guess is where calls go to die.

signals.note: You appear in local searches, but listings do not agree on where you are. Channel Road, Highway 8 Business, and Casa Grande all show up in the wild.
signals.next: Claim or clean the Google listing so there is one pin. Hide or mark the old addresses as moved.

signals.note: The phone (619) 443-3647 is the one thing that stays consistent. That is the porch light that still works.
signals.next: Keep that number on every listing. If someone else has an old one posted, get it taken down.

signals.note: Instagram says Tuesday through Saturday 9 to 4, Sunday 10 to 2 for DIY. Facebook says by appointment only. Both can be true. They do not read as true together.
signals.next: Write one sentence: when you take appointments, when DIY is open. Put that sentence in all three places.

signals.note: Instagram has life in it. The public listings do not clearly show the new Channel Road shop the way a stranger would need.
signals.next: Shoot the storefront, the tubs, and two freshly done dogs this week. Put the same three photos on Google.

signals.note: The domain listed as the shop website does not load the shop. It currently shows unrelated pages. That is not a small rot. It is a broken front door.
signals.next: Take the old domain off Yelp and Google until you own a page that is actually yours. A simple one-pager beats a hijacked URL.

signals.note: Name is close. Phone is good. Address is a mess. Three locations in the public record is how people drive to the wrong lot.
signals.next: Pick 9838 Channel Road if that is home now. Make every listing say that, and only that.
